key_insight: Quantum classifiers do not help uniformly on natural-image tasks; their success depends strongly on whether the input representation geometry aligns with the quantum feature space.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum ML pipelines, the main design choice is not only the quantum classifier, but also selecting or learning classical features that are compatible with quantum inductive biases.
method: Used classical feature extractors to provide strong representations for natural images.
Compared quantum classifiers under controlled data scale and supervision strength.
Analyzed representation geometry and kernel alignment to assess compatibility with quantum feature spaces.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates quantum classifiers on classical visual benchmarks using controlled scaling and supervision settings to isolate the effect of representation geometry.
watch_item: A quantum classifier may appear weak if the upstream classical features are misaligned with its inductive bias, so feature compatibility must be checked before attributing poor performance to the quantum model itself.
paper_title: Representation Geometry and Inductive Biases in Quantum Classifiers across Classical Visual Benchmarks
